sources.title: Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, second edition
sources.locator: Complete 651-page book inspected. Chapter 12, Sections 12.2–12.6: printed pp. 327–353. In particular, the full proof of Theorem 12.1 and Lemmas 12.3–12.4, the MFCQ definition, and the complete proofs of Theorems 12.5–12.6.

contents.name: LICQ KKT existence, equality and inequality multiplier signs, and uniqueness under LICQ
contents.reason: The carrier proves existence locally under MFCQ, derives LICQ implies MFCQ by an explicit right-inverse argument, and proves uniqueness from independence of active gradients.

contents.name: MFCQ definition and first-order multiplier theorem boundary
contents.reason: The book states MFCQ and notes that a first-order KKT theorem extends to it, but does not give the proof; this carrier supplies the tangent-cone and Farkas proof in full.

contents.name: Critical cone characterization by positive multipliers
contents.reason: The carrier proves the complementary-slackness and linearized-cone equivalence directly in the repository's g_i <= 0 convention.

contents.name: Second-order necessary condition on critical directions
contents.reason: The full source proof uses LICQ and feasible directions; this carrier supplies a local second-order-jet lemma and checks the active multiplier branches explicitly.

contents.name: Second-order sufficient condition on the critical cone
contents.reason: The source theorem requires KKT and strict positivity only on nonzero critical directions, with no constraint qualification; the local proof preserves that boundary.

contents.name: Failed constraint qualification at a genuine local minimizer
contents.reason: The source illustrates failure of linearization at a degenerate feasible point; the local example independently verifies a C2 global minimizer with no multipliers.

contents.name: Active-set quadratic KKT certificate
contents.reason: The local example computes feasibility, active set, LICQ, the multiplier, stationarity, and the unique global minimum exactly.

contents.name: KKT stationarity does not by itself prove a minimum
contents.reason: The local saddle example checks the KKT point and its negative critical curvature directly.

sources.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
sources.locator: Complete 714-page author-hosted book inspected. Chapter 2, Section 2.5.1, printed pp. 50–51; Chapter 3, Section 3.1.3; Chapter 5, Sections 5.1–5.3.2, printed pp. 215–236; Section 5.8, printed pp. 263–264.

contents.name: Euclidean projection, variational inequality, and separation
contents.reason: The source supplies the Euclidean projection/separation setting; the exact Farkas alternative is proved locally by projection onto the closed finite cone.

contents.name: Finite generated-cone closure required before projection
contents.reason: The source notes this closure issue but does not use it as an unproved premise here; the local proof reduces supports to independent subsets and proves closedness.

contents.name: Convex gradient inequality and KKT global certificate
contents.reason: The source's convex KKT argument is reflected in the carrier, which writes the signed g_i <= 0 calculation and normal-cone conclusion.

contents.name: Weak duality for every dual feasible multiplier
contents.reason: The local proof is the complete one-line Lagrangian lower-bound argument with the declared sign convention.

contents.name: Relative-interior Slater condition and dual attainment
contents.reason: Boyd's full proof assumes ambient interior of the effective domain and full equality rank; this carrier proves the stated relative-interior form on the actual affine image and includes dependent-domain geometry.

contents.name: Relative-interior support for the perturbation value function
contents.reason: The source invokes a separating-hyperplane/subgradient result; this carrier proves the needed finite-dimensional support fact locally from projection and continuity.

contents.name: Positive duality-gap boundary example
contents.reason: The local example closes the source's open perspective domain at its finite boundary and verifies the unchanged primal and dual values.

sources.title: Zhiyuan Li, Convex Optimization, Lecture 5: Lagrange Multipliers and KKT
sources.locator: Full 551-line lecture inspected. Theorem 5.1, lines 72–84; Theorems 5.3–5.4 and the complete Slater proof, lines 193–333; Example 5.5, lines 418–446.

contents.name: Weak-duality certificate
contents.reason: The source gives Theorem 5.1 and its proof; the carrier reproduces the lower-bound reasoning under the page's explicit extended-domain convention.

contents.name: Slater strong duality and dual attainment
contents.reason: The lecture's full proof invokes a relative-interior perturbation subgradient theorem; the local carrier proves that support result itself and verifies the affine-image and nontrivial-constraint hypotheses.

contents.name: Positive-gap example when Slater fails
contents.reason: The source's Example 5.5 supplies the model; the local example adds the closed perspective boundary point and proves properness, closed convexity, attainment, and the exact gap.

contents.name: Failure of constraint qualification and missing multipliers
contents.reason: The B example gives its own C2 feasibility and stationarity refutation.

contents.name: KKT stationary saddle
contents.reason: The B example verifies the gradient, Hessian, and both positive and negative nearby objective directions directly.

sources.locator: Full lecture inspected; Example 5.5 and its exact primal and dual value calculations, lines 418–446.

contents.reason: The local example extends the source perspective function by its closed finite boundary value and verifies the dual infimum along explicit sequences.
